node.title: E22 two-class exhaustion for worst-word challengers
node.statement: At the relevant low-slack crossing radii, every non-planted list word for the planted sunflower receiver lies in the structured E15 challenger class: mixed-petal or full-petal. Equivalently, after planted words are removed, there is no one-petal-only or background/core-only third challenger class. The proof uses root-count localization and the ratio-flat obstruction: a third-class word would need to replace r core roots by background roots with r < ell, but constancy on an ell-point petal would force a degree-r polynomial to vanish on ell distinct points, so the replacement is empty and the word is planted.
node.attack_surface: complete the E22 census remotely or prove directly from the interpolation/agreement equations that any non-planted crossing codeword touching at most one petal cannot reach agreement k+sigma
node.falsifier: an exhaustive cell with unclassified > 0, or an explicit low-slack word family outside planted plus mixed/full-petal classes
